title: Level a production mix in a heijunka box
instruction: Load the heijunka box to level the production mix: put one kanban in each of the six pockets, with the red kanbans in every other pocket so that no two neighbouring pockets hold the same colour.
context: Lean plants level the product mix over a shift (heijunka) instead of running each product in one batch, which smooths demand on upstream processes and inventory. This is a simplified single-row levelling board, one kanban per time slot. It tests turning a stated levelling rule into a placement order that differs from the order the kanbans arrive in.
setup: The table top is 74.75 cm above the floor. Two arms 61 cm apart on the table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm. A dark grey painted steel heijunka box is fixed across the far side of the table at x = 34: a 4 mm floor plate (7 x 37 cm) with six square pockets, 5 cm inside, in a row along y at y = 15, 9, 3, -3, -9 and -15 (slot 1 at y = 15), divided by 1 cm walls that reach 1.5 cm above the table (1.1 cm above the pocket floor). A grey aluminium tray, 5 cm along x by 30 cm along y and 4 mm thick, lies on the table at x = 18. Six kanbans, plastic 3 cm cubes of 40 g each standing in for kanban cards in their holders, stand on the tray grouped by product: red (product A) at y = 12.5, 7.5 and 2.5; blue (B) at -2.5 and -7.5; yellow (C) at -12.5.
scoring: A pocket is filled when exactly one released kanban sits in it: its centre inside the pocket's walls and its underside within 1 cm of the pocket floor. A kanban resting on another one, or on a wall, doesn't count, and a pocket holding two counts as unfilled. The box is levelled when all six pockets are filled and the three red kanbans are in alternate pockets (1, 3, 5 or 2, 4, 6), so no two neighbouring pockets match. Score = 0.3 x filled pockets / 6 + 0.7 if levelled. The start scores 0; three filled pockets 0.15; all six in tray order (red, red, red, blue, blue, yellow) 0.3; 1.0 for a levelled box, for example red, blue, red, yellow, red, blue, and the trial then ends once it has held for 1 s. Levelling is credited only for the full box, so a full box with a mistake (0.3) scores more than a correct box with one pocket empty (0.25). Filling in a random order averages 0.37. Orientation doesn't matter. Anything the rules above don't cover (for example a kanban dropped off the table) counts neither way. On real arms, read each pocket's colour from a top-down photo of the end state, and check from a side photo that no kanban rests on another or on a wall.
reset_notes: Stand the kanbans back on the tray in their groups.
fidelity: Approximate. The kanbans are coloured plastic blocks rather than cards in holders, so they are easier to grip than real cards. The box is a single row with one kanban per slot; a real heijunka box has a row per product and can hold several cards per slot. The simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
